mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds Rate remains persistently below its pre-pandemic median for at least 3 consecutive months, it reduces the real discount rate applied to expected future cash flows, thereby boosting S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Over 60-day horizon, SPX 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from the 30-day moving average return during similar low-rate periods (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) accompanied by a simultaneous decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strengthening labor market, which raises consumer confidence and equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by >10% month-over-month AND UNRATE falls by >0.2 percentage points in the same month
failure_condition: In 20-day windows where the trigger occurs, SPX 20-day forward returns are negative or flat, and the 20-day realized volatility is higher than the 5-day average during recovery periods (Rank IC < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in industrial production (INDPRO) above its 12-month moving average, sustained for two consecutive months, indicates strengthening supply-side demand, which typically precedes equity market strength and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days.
failure_condition: During qualifying INDPRO upswings, SPX 5-day forward returns are negative and the 5-day realized volatility is lower than the 30-day average during prior expansion phases (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in consumer inflation measured by CPIAUCSL (month-on-month decline of >1.5%) combined with a decline in the goods price index (not directly observable here, but implied by CPIAUCSL behavior) suggests deflationary pressure, which historically precedes equity risk-on flows and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: In 20-day windows following CPIAUCSL deflation, SPX 20-day forward returns are negative or flat, and the 20-day realized Sharpe ratio is below the 5-year average during deflationary episodes (Rank IC < 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: When the monthly real personal consumption expenditure billings (implied by GDPC1) exceeds the prior year's January value by at least 5% in the current month, it indicates strong demand for credit and financing, prompting the Fed to keep rates steady and supporting equity valuations, which predicts positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 > GDPC1_prev_year_Jan by >5% in current month
failure_condition: During such GDPC1 spikes, SPX 60-day forward returns are not statistically superior to the 60-day historical average during non-crisis periods (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4.0% followed by a sustained rise in labor market participation (implied by PAYEMS) suggests a labor market tightness effect that boosts consumer spending and corporate profits, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 4.0 AND PAYEMS increases by >5% month-over-month
failure_condition: During such labor market transitions, SPX 20-day forward returns are negative and the 20-day realized beta to the S&P 500 labor index (from FRED) is below -0.5 (indicating underperformance).

mechanism_narrative: A prolonged decline in consumer inflation (CPIAUCSL) coupled with a sustained drop in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for three consecutive months signals a supply-side shock, which typically precedes equity risk aversion reversal and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL < CPIAUCSL_12month_moving_avg AND INDPRO < INDPRO_12month_moving_avg for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: During such supply shocks, SPX 60-day forward returns are not statistically higher than the 60-day average during prior non-shock periods (Rank IC < 0.2).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in the S&P 500 VIX (not directly observable here, but proxy via market implied volatility proxies such as FEDFUNDS behavior and risk-off flows) combined with a sustained decline in FEDFUNDS for two consecutive months predicts risk-off to risk-on rotation in equities, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days in risk-sensitive regimes.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS decreases by >0.25% for 2 consecutive months AND SPX implied volatility (derived from options) is above 20-day moving average
failure_condition: During such risk-off-to-risk-on shifts, SPX 5-day forward returns are negative and the 5-day realized volatility premium over the 1-month risk-free rate is below historical averages (t-test p > 0.05).
